title: Digital Audio Representation
description: Sample rate, bit depth and PCM as the substrate everything else sits on — why 16 kHz is the ASR convention and 24 kHz the TTS one, what Nyquist actually forbids, and how a naive resample between them introduces aliasing that a vocoder faithfully reproduces as a metallic buzz.
viz: waveform sampler with a sample-rate slider from 4 kHz to 48 kHz reconstructing a swept sine, showing the aliased frequency folding back below Nyquist as the rate drops, with the original and reconstructed spectra overlaid

title: Spectrograms and the Mel Scale
description: The STFT as the bridge from waveform to image — window length trading time resolution against frequency resolution, hop length setting the frame rate every downstream model inherits, and mel filterbanks compressing linear frequency onto a perceptual scale so 80 bins carry what 1024 FFT bins did.
viz: live STFT of a spoken utterance with draggable window and hop length, showing the time-frequency smearing tradeoff, plus a toggle overlaying the mel filterbank triangles and the resulting 80-bin mel spectrogram

title: Telephony Audio Constraints
description: Why a model that sounds excellent in the demo degrades on an actual phone call: 8 kHz narrowband truncating every fricative, G.711 mu-law quantisation, Opus at low bitrate, and the fact that a 24 kHz TTS voice downsampled to a PSTN leg loses exactly the band that carries intelligibility of s, f and th.
viz: A/B player synthesising the same utterance at 24 kHz, 16 kHz and 8 kHz mu-law with the spectra stacked, highlighting the energy above 3.4 kHz that the phone network discards and marking which phonemes lose their discriminating cue

title: Jitter, Packet Loss and Concealment
description: What the network does to audio between your synthesiser and the caller's ear — jitter buffers trading latency for smoothness, packet loss concealment interpolating gaps, and why a TTS stream that emits large chunks is far more fragile to a lost packet than one emitting small ones.
viz: simulated RTP stream with sliders for jitter variance, loss rate and buffer depth, showing playout underruns as audible gaps and plotting the added latency the buffer costs against the dropout rate it prevents

title: Voice Activity Detection and Endpointing
description: Deciding when speech starts and stops — energy and zero-crossing baselines against neural VAD, and the asymmetric cost that defines the tuning: a premature endpoint cuts the caller off mid-sentence, a late one leaves dead air that reads as the agent being broken.
viz: waveform with a live VAD trace and adjustable hangover, silence threshold and minimum-speech duration, scoring false cut-offs against added latency as the thresholds move

title: Text Normalization for Speech
description: The unglamorous front end that decides whether '$1.5M on 3/4/26' is read correctly — number and date expansion, abbreviation handling, and homograph disambiguation where 'read', 'live' and 'lead' need part-of-speech context the acoustic model never sees.
viz: text box running a normalization pipeline stage by stage, showing the intermediate expansions and letting the reader inject ambiguous strings to watch which stage resolves or mangles them

title: Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion
description: Turning orthography into pronunciation — lexicon lookup for the common case, a learned G2P model for out-of-vocabulary words and names, and why IPA versus ARPAbet is a real engineering choice rather than notation preference when you mix datasets.
viz: word input showing lexicon hit or model fallback, the predicted phoneme sequence in both ARPAbet and IPA, and a set of adversarial proper nouns where the model and lexicon disagree

title: Prosody: Pitch, Duration and Energy
description: The three signals that separate speech from a talking clock — F0 contour carrying intonation and question versus statement, per-phoneme duration carrying rhythm and emphasis, and energy carrying stress, plus why predicting them explicitly gives control that an end-to-end model buries.
viz: sentence with per-phoneme pitch, duration and energy tracks the reader can drag, resynthesising the contour so the same words shift between statement, question and emphatic reading

title: Forced Alignment
description: Recovering which audio frames correspond to which phonemes when you have the transcript but no timings — Viterbi alignment over an HMM, CTC-based alignment, and Montreal Forced Aligner in practice, the labelling step every duration predictor is trained on.
viz: utterance with a transcript, animating the Viterbi trellis as it finds the lowest-cost monotonic path and drawing the resulting phoneme boundaries onto the spectrogram, with a control to corrupt the transcript and watch the alignment fail

title: Tacotron 2
description: The autoregressive encoder-attention-decoder that made neural TTS work — character or phoneme encoder, location-sensitive attention, and a decoder emitting mel frames one step at a time, with a stop token deciding when the utterance ends.
viz: step-through of the decoder emitting mel frames, showing the attention alignment matrix building diagonally and the stop-token probability rising, pausable at any frame

title: Attention Failure Modes in TTS
description: The characteristic ways autoregressive TTS breaks — skipped words, repeated syllables and babbling that never terminates — all readable as a non-monotonic attention matrix, and the fixes: location-sensitive attention, monotonic constraints, and windowing.
viz: gallery of real alignment matrices for healthy, skipping, repeating and collapsed synthesis, with the corresponding audio artifact described and a control forcing monotonicity to show the failure disappear

title: FastSpeech 2
description: Non-autoregressive synthesis that removes attention from the decode path — an explicit duration predictor and length regulator expanding phonemes to frames in one shot, with variance adaptors injecting pitch and energy, trading a little naturalness for constant-time generation.
viz: side-by-side of autoregressive versus length-regulated decoding on the same phoneme sequence, showing the duration predictor's expansion factors and how editing one phoneme's duration stretches only that segment

title: Autoregressive vs Non-Autoregressive TTS
description: The trade that decides your architecture: autoregressive models generally sound better and can be streamed early but have unbounded per-utterance latency and can fail to terminate, while non-autoregressive models give predictable latency and parallel decode at the cost of prosodic variety.
viz: latency simulator plotting time-to-first-audio and total synthesis time for both families against utterance length, with a variance band showing the tail risk of an autoregressive model failing to emit a stop token

title: VITS and End-to-End TTS
description: Collapsing the mel intermediate entirely — a conditional VAE with normalizing flows and adversarial training that maps text to waveform in one model, with stochastic duration prediction giving the rhythm variation that deterministic predictors flatten.
viz: diagram of the VITS training path versus inference path with the flow and discriminator branches, plus a sampler drawing several stochastic durations for the same sentence so the reader hears the prosodic variation

title: WaveNet and Autoregressive Audio
description: The model that proved raw-waveform generation was possible — dilated causal convolutions giving an exponentially growing receptive field over 16,000 samples per second, and the reason nobody serves it directly: one forward pass per sample.
viz: animated dilated convolution stack showing the receptive field doubling per layer, with a counter of forward passes required per second of audio to make the inference cost concrete

title: Griffin-Lim and Phase Reconstruction
description: Why a mel spectrogram is not enough to invert — magnitude discards phase, and Griffin-Lim iteratively guesses it, producing the characteristic robotic smear that motivated neural vocoders in the first place. Still worth knowing as the zero-dependency fallback.
viz: iteration slider running Griffin-Lim from 1 to 100 rounds, playing the reconstruction at each stage and plotting spectral convergence so the reader hears the artifact shrink but never disappear

title: HiFi-GAN
description: The vocoder that made neural TTS deployable — a fully convolutional generator with multi-receptive-field fusion, trained against multi-period and multi-scale discriminators that catch the periodic structure of voiced speech, running far faster than real time on a GPU.
viz: diagram of the multi-period discriminator reshaping the waveform at several periods, with a control showing which artifacts each discriminator scale is responsible for suppressing

title: Neural Audio Codecs and RVQ
description: EnCodec and SoundStream compressing speech to a handful of discrete tokens per frame via residual vector quantization — the representation that lets a language model generate audio at all, and the bitrate-quality curve that decides how many codebooks you carry.
viz: residual quantization walkthrough showing each codebook stage reducing the residual, with a bitrate slider trading codebook count against reconstruction quality and the token rate the downstream LM must model

title: Streaming TTS
description: Emitting audio before the sentence is synthesised — chunking at clause boundaries, overlap-add across chunk seams, and the lookahead a vocoder needs, because time-to-first-audio is what the caller experiences as responsiveness, not total synthesis time.
viz: timeline comparing batch and streaming synthesis of the same sentence, marking time-to-first-audio for each and letting the reader shrink the chunk size to watch first-audio drop while seam artifacts appear

title: Latency Budget Decomposition
description: Where a voice agent's response time actually goes — endpointing hangover, ASR finalisation, LLM time-to-first-token, TTS time-to-first-audio, and network legs — decomposed against the roughly 800 ms at which a caller starts to perceive the pause as dead air.
viz: stacked latency budget with adjustable per-stage values, flagging which stages are serial and which can overlap, and marking the perceptual thresholds where the conversation starts to feel broken

title: Barge-In and Interruption Detection
description: Letting the caller talk over the agent — detecting speech while audio is playing, distinguishing a genuine interruption from a backchannel 'mhm', cancelling in-flight synthesis, and truncating the LLM context to what the caller actually heard rather than what you generated.
viz: duplex timeline with agent output and caller input on separate tracks, letting the reader trigger an interruption at any point and showing what is cancelled, what was already played, and what the context must be truncated to

title: Turn-Taking and Endpointing Policy
description: Deciding the caller has finished — fixed silence thresholds against semantic endpointing that reads whether the utterance is syntactically complete, and the asymmetry that makes this hard: interrupting a thinking caller costs more than a short wait.
viz: transcript arriving word by word with both a fixed-timeout and a semantic endpointer running in parallel, showing where they disagree on utterances with mid-sentence pauses

title: Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Models
description: The alternative to the ASR-LLM-TTS cascade — models consuming and emitting audio tokens directly, preserving paralinguistics the cascade throws away and collapsing three latencies into one, against the cascade's debuggability, swappable components and text-level control.
viz: side-by-side pipeline diagram with per-stage latency and the information each cascade boundary discards, plus a decision table of which failure modes each architecture makes easier or harder to diagnose

title: Real-Time Factor and GPU Sizing
description: Capacity planning for concurrent calls — real-time factor as the unit of measure, how batching raises throughput while raising time-to-first-audio, and deriving the GPU count for a target concurrency from RTF, batch size and the arrival distribution.
viz: capacity calculator taking concurrent calls, RTF and batch size, deriving required GPUs and showing the queueing delay that appears as utilisation approaches saturation

title: Speaker Embeddings
description: Representing who is speaking as a fixed vector — d-vectors and x-vectors trained for speaker discrimination, used to condition a multi-speaker synthesiser, and the same embedding reused as the similarity metric when you evaluate a cloned voice.
viz: 2-D projection of a speaker embedding space with several speakers and multiple utterances each, showing within-speaker clustering and letting the reader interpolate between two speakers to hear the blended voice

title: Zero-Shot Voice Cloning
description: Cloning a voice from seconds of reference audio — codec language models in the VALL-E shape treating TTS as conditional token continuation, why this generalises to unseen speakers where embedding-conditioned models do not, and how reference quality bounds the result.
viz: pipeline from reference clip to acoustic tokens to generated tokens to waveform, with controls for reference length and noise showing how similarity degrades as the prompt gets shorter or dirtier

title: Emotion and Style Control
description: Controlling how something is said independently of who says it — reference encoders and global style tokens learning an unsupervised basis of speaking styles, and the entanglement problem where style transfer drags speaker identity along with it.
viz: grid of global style tokens with per-token weights the reader can mix, showing the resulting prosody contour and flagging when a style change has also shifted the speaker embedding

title: Watermarking, Consent and Voice Safety
description: The obligations that come with cloning a voice — audio watermarking that survives codec transcoding, consent capture and provenance for training data, disclosure that a caller is speaking to a synthetic voice, and treating recorded voice as PHI in a healthcare setting.
viz: watermark robustness matrix showing detection rate after mu-law transcoding, resampling, noise and clipping, alongside a consent and retention checklist mapped to the pipeline stage where each obligation binds

title: MOS, CMOS and Subjective Evaluation
description: The listening tests that remain the ground truth for naturalness — absolute MOS against comparative CMOS, how many raters and utterances you need for a difference to be real, and the biases that make an uncontrolled MOS number close to meaningless.
viz: MOS simulator drawing ratings from two systems with adjustable true difference and rater count, showing the confidence interval narrowing and how often an underpowered test reports the wrong winner

title: Objective Metrics for TTS
description: The automatic proxies you can run in CI — mel cepstral distortion for spectral accuracy, WER through an ASR model for intelligibility, and speaker-embedding cosine for cloning similarity, plus where each diverges from what listeners actually report.
viz: scatter of each objective metric against held-out MOS across synthetic systems, showing correlation and the outlier systems where a metric confidently disagrees with human raters

title: Serving Cost Economics for TTS
description: Cost per minute of synthesised speech — GPU-seconds per audio-second from RTF, the effect of batching and caching frequently repeated phrases, and the build-versus-buy crossover against per-character vendor pricing at a given call volume.
viz: cost model taking call volume, average call length, RTF and instance price, plotting self-hosted cost per minute against vendor pricing and marking the crossover volume

title: Regression Testing a Voice Agent
description: Keeping a deployed voice agent honest — golden audio sets replayed through the full ASR-LLM-TTS loop, asserting on transcript and timing rather than waveform bytes, and catching the compounding drift where an ASR upgrade silently changes what the agent hears.
viz: regression dashboard replaying a golden call set across two pipeline versions, diffing transcripts, endpoint timings and time-to-first-audio, and flagging which stage introduced each regression
